recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reverting to the seed's interim 'possibly accompanied' wording would discard the later accepted FHIR-27051 refinement without improving the 401/403 behavior.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I issue asking to clarify that HTTP 401/403 search failures do not always require an OperationOutcome, because security frameworks or other non-FHIR-aware layers may reject requests before the FHIR server can return a resource.
initial_application: Commit b05c3d81668ddaef25eac26202e9ade43f3a9b69 applied FHIR-30240 by changing the old search-failure text from requiring a 4xx/5xx response with OperationOutcome to saying the status code could be possibly accompanied by an OperationOutcome.
additional_context: The initiating Zulip thread and 2021-02-22 FHIR-I minutes support making OperationOutcome optional for this case. Later Published issue FHIR-27051 refined the same sentence to the current rule: 4xx/5xx status is required for failed search, and OperationOutcome is SHOULD only when failure occurs at a FHIR-aware processing level.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/http.html now says OperationOutcome is not required for every HTTP 4xx/5xx response and the search-failure paragraph requires only a 4xx/5xx status code, with SHOULD guidance for FHIR-aware failures.

related_jiras.note: Later Published clarification on the same search-failure sentence; it superseded the seed's interim wording with the current FHIR-aware SHOULD guidance.
